| 6 | Maryland | $12,835 | Yes: $11,015 tuition plus $1,820 fees. | https://academiccatalog.umd.edu/undergraduate/fees-expenses-financial-aid/tuition-fees/ |

| 8 | Washington (Seattle) | $14,340 | Yes: $12,664 tuition plus $1,676 fees. | https://finance.uw.edu/tuition-fees/node/24790 |
| 9 | UCLA | $16,430 | Yes: $15,588 systemwide tuition plus $842 campus fees. | https://financialaid.ucla.edu/go/coa |
| 10 | Oregon | $17,474.85 | Yes: $14,531.85 tuition plus $2,943 fees. | https://pages.uoregon.edu/baoforms/files/brp/Fees/2026-2027%20Tuition%20and%20Fee%20Tables.pdf |
| 11 | Minnesota (Twin Cities) | $17,814.68 | Yes: $16,744 tuition plus $1,070.68 student services fee. | https://onestop.umn.edu/node/126 and https://ssf.umn.edu/ |
| 12 | Michigan State | $18,071 | Yes: $17,656 tuition plus $415 in required fees. | https://controller.msu.edu/student-accounts/tuition-rates-by-semester/resident-undergrad-fall-spring |
| 13 | Illinois (Urbana-Champaign) | $18,530 | Yes. This is the low end of a range, and I assume it is the base rate (see Notes). | https://admissions.illinois.edu/invest/tuition |

| 15 | Rutgers (New Brunswick) | $19,389 | Yes: $15,381 tuition plus $4,008 fees. | https://admissions.rutgers.edu/costs-and-aid/tuition-fees |
| 16 | Penn State (University Park) | $20,878 | No, tuition only. The mandatory Student Initiated Fee is extra, and I didn't find its amount. | https://tuition.psu.edu/rates-effective-2026-fall-semester |
| 17 | Northwestern | $73,062 | Yes: $71,802 tuition plus $1,260 fees. | https://news.northwestern.edu/stories/2026/05/northwestern-sets-tuition-and-fees-for-2026-2027-academic-year |
| 18 | USC | $77,336 | Yes: $75,384 tuition plus $1,952 fees. A $450 new-student fee is added in the first semester. | https://admission.usc.edu/?p=12825 |

**Notes and caveats**
- **Purdue:** I never reached the bursar rate table. The $9,992 comes from secondary sources and Purdue's tuition-freeze announcement. Treat it as unverified until you check the bursar tables. Penn State is the other school I couldn't fully confirm, because its published figure excludes fees.
- **Illinois:** The page gives only a range of $18,530 to $24,018, depending on major. I took the low end as the base rate. The fee schedule's $1,715 per semester implies about $15,100 in base tuition, which fits. Health insurance is not part of this figure.
- **Michigan:** The $9,448 per term is the proposed FY27 table's Fall 2026 rate, which I doubled. News coverage says the Regents approved about a 3% increase in June 2026, but I didn't see the final approved table.
- **Michigan State:** The Controller's page gave $8,828 tuition plus $207.50 in fees per semester, which I doubled. Program fees and section fees are excluded.
- **Minnesota:** The student services fee is $535.34 per semester on the fee site, but $532.50 on the One Stop fees page. I used $535.34.
- **UCLA:** The aid page says its figures may not be final. A search snippet showed $16,706 ($1,118 campus fees), while the page I fetched showed $16,430. Health insurance is excluded.
- **Washington:** The $1,676 in fees includes a one-time $467 orientation fee and the $243 U-PASS. UW's admissions pages show different figures ($13,406 and $13,873).
- **Oregon:** This excludes a one-time $569.89 matriculation fee.
- **Ohio State, Rutgers and Wisconsin:** Ohio State's figure is a news-release number I didn't verify against the registrar's Columbus fee table. Rutgers' $4,008 fee figure is described as an average and varies by program. Wisconsin's figure matches the Regents' release.
